summary: The controller never got to Task 1. After loading the SDD skill and running its pre-flight scan, it kept re-reading the 76 KB / 1032-line subagent-driven-development SKILL.md. Each read filled the 100k auto-compact window again. Claude Code then stopped the turn with "Autocompact is thrashing: the context refilled to the limit within 3 turns of the previous compact, 3 times in a row." No subagents were dispatched, nothing was implemented, no commits were made, and it never reached the finishing step.
reasoning: None of the acceptance criteria were met: no code, no tests, no commits, no reviews and no finishing step. The cause I observed was the controller repeatedly re-reading a very large skill file after compaction, which set off Claude Code's autocompact-thrashing stop. I did not steer the session; the agent stopped on its own and asked no questions.

observations.description: Compaction loop: the session log has 3 compact_boundary events. After each one the controller ran Read on subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md again: a full read, then offset 824 limit 210, then another full read, then a full read with allow_large:true. At 75,982 bytes the skill file plus plan.md (27.6 KB) is too big for a 100k autoCompactWindow, so every re-read filled the context again. Claude Code's thrash guard stopped the turn before any task work started. The reread-after-compaction behaviour this scenario measures produces a loop when the skill itself is this large.

Claude Code's own "Skills restored (hyperpowers:communication, hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development)" ran after each compaction. The controller still did a manual Read of SKILL.md on top of that, so the skill content was likely loaded twice per cycle.
The agent went idle after the thrashing message without telling the user anything about where things stood or what to do next. From a developer's point of view the session just stopped.

Startup: the workspace trust dialog has "No, exit" selected by default. A "Newer Opus model available (Currently pinned: Opus 5)" prompt also appeared even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed on the command line. I chose No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.

Consider shrinking the SDD SKILL.md, or having the reread step read only the relevant section and only once per compaction. As it stands, a reread instruction combined with a small compaction window can never make progress.

criteria.criterion: All four functions exported from src/textstats.js with test files, committed, and npm test passes
criteria.evidence: `cat src/textstats.js` → `module.exports = {};`. `ls test` is empty. `git log --oneline` HEAD is still `0867661 Add textstats fixture and implementation plan` (no new commits). npm test passes only because there are no tests.

criteria.criterion: Each task reviewed before the next starts
criteria.evidence: Running jq over the session log 26b2aa22-….jsonl for tool_use names shows only Skill, Bash and Read calls. There are no Agent/Task dispatches, so no implementer or reviewer subagents ever ran.

criteria.criterion: Final whole-branch review after last task
criteria.evidence: No tasks were done and the log has no Agent calls, so no final review happened.

The session ended on the screen message "Autocompact is thrashing: ... A file being read or a tool output is likely too large for the context window" followed by "Baked for 3m 15s". It never offered a finishing step (merge/keep/discard), and the agent asked no questions.
